# gitmoap_repository_pipeline_component_versions (Data Source)

List a component's published versions, newest first. Versions are ordered by version number rather than alphabetically, so v0.10.0 comes above v0.3.0. Filter by `lifecycle_state` (active, deprecated, sunset, or all, the default); pages hold up to 100 versions (20 by default) and continue with `next_token`. Anyone who can read the pipelines here may call it.

The token needs `pipeline:read`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "component_id" {
  type = string
}

data "gitmoap_repository_by_path" "api" {
  full_path = "acme/platform/api"
}

data "gitmoap_repository_pipeline_component_versions" "api" {
  component_id = var.component_id
  repo_id      = data.gitmoap_repository_by_path.api.repository_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `component_id` (String) The component's id
- `repo_id` (String) The repository's id

### Optional

- `lifecycle_state` (String) active, deprecated, sunset or all (default all)

### Read-Only

- `items` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items))

<a id="nestedatt--items"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items`

Read-Only:

- `capability_requirements` (List of String) The provider capabilities the version's steps use.
- `changelog` (String)
- `commit_sha` (String) The commit whose files it was published from.
- `contract_digest` (String) A SHA-256 fingerprint, in hex, of what a pipeline using the version must satisfy: its
parameters, its ports and the variables it reads. It changes only when that contract does.
- `depth` (Number) How many levels of components the version spans: 1 when it uses no other component.
- `expanded_node_count` (Number) How many steps the version expands into.
- `lifecycle_state` (String) Where a published version sits in its retirement.

A `deprecated` version still resolves for an exact reference and still runs, but no floating
reference selects it — which is what makes deprecating the safe way to retire one. A `sunset`
version refuses to resolve at all, exact reference included.
- `published_at` (String)
- `published_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--published_by))
- `tag_name` (String) The tag that published it: `<name>/<version>`, or a plain `<version>`. Absent on a version
published before versions were published by tag.
- `variable_requirements` (List of String) The variables the version's steps read from the pipeline that uses it. Each must be declared
on the environment those steps run in, or on a group or repository above the pipeline, or
a run is refused when it starts.
- `version` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--items--published_by"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.published_by`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor and empty on a redacted one.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor.
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.
